input.quote: Either Party may terminate this Agreement for any reason following the Initial Term upon ninety (90) days written notice to the other Party. Except for termination for material breach as detailed in paragraph 4(b), Kubient shall be entitled to all fees generated during the termination period regardless of which Party terminates the Agreement
input.rationale: Compliant at the fallback; no redline proposed. A Customer convenience right is present: Section 4(a) provides that "Either Party may terminate this Agreement for any reason following the Initial Term upon ninety (90) days written notice to the other Party." The "Either Party" phrasing includes AP, so AP holds a for-any-reason (convenience) exit on 90 days' notice — inside the fallback's 60-90 day window. The right is simply not drafted by naming the Customer, which is a phrasing point only and does not remove the right. Term length: the committed period is a one (1) year Initial Term that auto-renews in 1-year increments, so the detection trigger for "absence of any Customer convenience right in a term longer than 12 months" is not met, and a 1-year term with a 90-day exit is not a multi-year lock-in. Vendor side: Kubient's exit requires the same 90 days' notice, so it is not "fewer than 90 days" and does not reach walk-away; it is symmetric rather than one-sided against us, and the Initial Term lock-out prevents Kubient from exiting mid-term. Economics: Kubient's entitlement to fees "generated during the termination period" is bounded by the ~3-month notice period, consistent with the fallback cap of no more than 3 months' fees, and applies whichever party terminates. Noted but not flagged as deviations: notice is 90 days rather than the preferred 30; Kubient's convenience right is not confined to term-end; and there is no pro-rata prepaid-fee refund, which is inapplicable because Section 5 is a revenue-share under which Kubient remits to AP rather than AP prepaying fees.
